source: Wu et al. (2024) Mind's Eye of LLMs: Visualization-of-Thought
finding: VoT asks a text-only model to draw the state of the world as text after each step, like a mental image. It beat plain chain-of-thought on grid-world spatial tasks with GPT-4.
numbers: GPT-4 table (column labels garbled in extraction): CoT 37.02/9.48/48.61/54.15/54.00; no-viz 37.17/10.28/48.49/46.98/35.50; VoT 40.77/14.72/55.28/63.94/59.00. VoT beat no-viz by 23.5% on natural-language navigation. Datasets: 200 maps, 2,520 QA, 796 tiling items.
limits: Needs strong models. Tracking is prompt-sensitive. 2D grids only.
agent_relevance: Direct test of O6: write the intermediate state as a grid. Cheap, no training.
quote: Both mental images and visual state tracking rely on the emergent ability of advanced LLMs.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Mind's Eye of LLMs: Visualization-of-Thought (weaker models)
finding: On weak models VoT gives little or nothing. LLaMA3-70B gains clearly; GPT-3.5 and LLaMA3-8B do not.
limits: Column mapping uncertain. Single runs.
agent_relevance: Use state-drawing only with strong models; test per model before enabling.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Mind's Eye of LLMs: Visualization-of-Thought (ring and tracking analysis)
finding: VoT is not always better. On a ring navigation variant it lost slightly. Models often fail to actually draw the state, and the drawing is often wrong.
numbers: Ring size 12, 200 instances: CoT 52.5% vs VoT 49.5%. Adding 'use ascii-art' raised complete tracking to 98.5% (+78.5) and task score to 62.5% (+3.5). Visual tiling: prompt compliance 51-52%, state accuracy 24-26%; when drawing was accurate, decisions correct 65-77%.
limits: Task-specific. Small n per condition.
agent_relevance: Check the drawn state in code (G2/G3) instead of trusting it. Accuracy of the image matters more than its presence.

source: Li et al. (2025) Imagine while Reasoning in Space: MVoT
finding: A multimodal model that generates an image of each step beats text chain-of-thought where text fails (FrozenLake) but loses where text can hold exact coordinates (Maze, MiniBehavior).
numbers: Anole-7B Maze/MiniBehavior/FrozenLake: Direct .717/.725/.779; CoT with layout .979/.981/.615; MVoT .930/.951/.856. GPT-4o: Direct .710/.458/.498; CoT .739/.468/.466; with visual thought .856/.644/.802.
limits: Image generation adds inference cost. Generated images sometimes show irrelevant detail and miss the intended change.
agent_relevance: Evidence for a mixed rule: symbolic form for exact lookup, spatial form for layout-heavy tracking. Not one form always.

source: Li et al. (2025) Imagine while Reasoning in Space: MVoT (scaling and ablation)
finding: Text reasoning degrades with grid size on FrozenLake; image reasoning stays flat. 90.8% of CoT's FrozenLake errors came from wrong hole coordinates. Image quality loss matters.
numbers: FrozenLake CoT 3x3 .940, 4x4 .723, 5x5 .500, 6x6 .391; MVoT .862, .840, .838, .888. Token discrepancy loss: Maze acc .9295 vs .7468 without; MiniBehavior .9514 vs .7228. CoT+MVoT oracle upper bound: Maze .998, MiniBehavior 1.00, FrozenLake .925.
limits: Single trained 7B model. The oracle bound is not a usable method.
agent_relevance: Complementarity: oracle gain suggests choosing representation per instance (code-checked) could beat either alone.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Is a Picture Worth a Thousand Words? (SpatialEval)
finding: Pictures often do not help. Text-only LLMs beat or match vision-language models on spatial tasks, and adding an image to text helps little when text already has the clues.
numbers: Spatial-Grid: GPT-4o TQA .986, VQA .833, VTQA .989; Claude 3 Opus TQA .957, VQA .455, VTQA .888; GPT-4V .923/.668/.924. Spatial-Map GPT-4o .616/.617/.643. Maze-Nav GPT-4o .353/.410/.382. Spatial-Real: LLaMA-3-8B text .884 vs VLM image-only .329-.445.
limits: Chance is 0.25 (derived). Synthetic tasks. Spatial-Real text was a 1,000-word caption, so the text carried the answer.
agent_relevance: Spatial form is not automatically better for a text model. For a grid with named cells, text wins. Pictorial form needs a visual encoder that works.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Is a Picture Worth a Thousand Words? (SpatialEval) (blind and noisy image ablations)
finding: Removing the image, or replacing it with noise, often raised VLM accuracy. This is evidence that the image channel can add noise.
numbers: LLaVA-1.6-34B Spatial-Grid: no image +20.1% over original image. LLaVA-1.6-Vicuna-13B Maze-Nav: noise image +6.5%. Modality gap VTQA minus VQA: 7.0% synthetic, 30.0% Spatial-Real. GPT-4V Spatial-Grid VQA to VTQA +25.6%.
limits: Exact values only in figures. Open-source models near chance anyway.
agent_relevance: Never assume a second representation is additive. Keep a text-only arm as control.

source: Wu et al. (2025) SpatiaLite: Imagine in Space
finding: Frontier models fail visual-centric mental tasks and fall back on language. Mental rotation is near floor even for the best reasoning model, while symbolic tasks like cube rolling are solved.
numbers: Mental Rotation: human 100; Gemini 2.5 Pro 20.5; o1 7.5; o4-mini 6.4; GPT-4o 4.7. Cube Rolling: o1 97.5, o4-mini 98.3, human 85.3. Tokens exceed 10,000 on hard items. Qwen-2.5-VL-7B Cube Rolling 12.5 to 42.3 with imagery plus reasoning distillation; Move Box and Wood Slide stay 0.
limits: Synthetic benchmark. Training result is for one 7B model.
agent_relevance: Models solve problems that can be recoded symbolically and fail when real spatial transformation is needed. Offload spatial transforms to code.

source: Wu et al. (2025) SpatiaLite input modality
finding: Text-only, image-only, and both formats give mixed results by model and task. Image input helped Gemini 2.5 Pro but not o4-mini.
numbers: o4-mini Rubik's VTQA 74.5% at 6.6k tokens; o4-mini Wood Slide VQA 4.5%. Gemini 2.5 Pro Wood Slide: VQA 50.6% at 9.5k tokens, TQA 48.5% at 12.3k, VTQA 52.3%.
limits: Single table, no seeds reported.
agent_relevance: Representation choice is model-specific; measure it per model.

source: Limits of Spatial Imagery Reasoning in Frontier LLMs (2026)
finding: Giving GPT-5.2 an external 3D 'imagery module' (a renderer it can rotate step by step) did not close the gap to humans. Authors call it a functional spatial-imagery deficit.
numbers: SpatialViz 3D rotation: human 79.16%; GPT-5.2 direct 50.00%; with imagery module 50-62.5% (10 runs); gpt-5.4 45-52%. Reset-to-canonical-view condition 85-97.5%. At 15 degrees GPT-5.2 got 1 of 6 directions right. Image models asked for a 30-degree view all returned the original.
limits: Small samples (40 problems, 80 pairs). Model names inconsistent in text. Metaphor only, no claim about human aphantasia.
agent_relevance: A renderer tool alone is not enough; the model inspects static views and does not simulate motion. Canonical views (reset) helped a lot, so give fixed re-anchoring views.

source: Visual serial processing deficits explain divergences in human and VLM reasoning (2025)
finding: VLM accuracy falls as human reaction time rises, a serial-processing signature like Kosslyn's scanning-time findings. Tool use helps when objects can be cropped.
numbers: Mental rotation (3,744 trials): human 79.6%, NoCoT 56.7%, CoT 56.9%, reasoning 58.1%; o3 with tools 88.8% vs 47.8% NoCoT on 400 hard trials. RT vs model accuracy r=-0.88 (rotation), -0.73 (Geoclidean), -0.97 (numerosity). Overlapping uniform objects: tools 10.0% vs 9.5%.
limits: Human RT is a proxy for serial load. Rotation tools gain may come from code, not imagery.
agent_relevance: Chain-of-thought does not fix rotation; code tools do. Route rotation and counting to code (O6).

source: Human Cognitive Benchmarks Reveal Foundational Visual Gaps in MLLMs (VisFactor, 2025)
finding: On 20 classic psychometric visualization tests (the human spatial-ability battery), 39 frontier models trail students. Mental rotation is a consistent failure. CoT is marginal and can hurt.
numbers: Best model 55.9% vs human 78.8% (31 students); Cronbach alpha 0.94; chance 2.89%. Gemini best 54.0%. CoT hurt on P3, CS2, SS3, VZ1. Temperature 0.5 and 1.0: little change.
limits: Page read through first 100k characters only. Model names as printed in the paper.
agent_relevance: Same kind of tests used in human imagery-ability research; an LLM that must do rotation should not trust itself.

source: Visual Planning: Let's Think Only with Images (2025)
finding: Training an image-only model to plan in pictures beats text reasoning on grid navigation and holds up as grids grow.
numbers: Avg exact match: LVM-7B VPRL 80.6 vs Qwen2.5-VL-7B SFT 53.6 (+27.0), Gemini 2.5 Pro think 43.7, Gemini 2.0 Flash CoT 12.8. FrozenLake EM Gemini 2.5 Pro 98.0 (3x3) to 38.8 (6x6); VPRL 97.6 to 82.4. Text variants with coordinates 74.4, ASCII 73.1, SFT direct 68.6 on FrozenLake.
limits: Needs trained image model. OOD larger grids collapse: FrozenLake 7x7 VPRL 20.4 EM; MiniBehavior 9x9 0.4.
agent_relevance: Strong claim for pictorial reasoning in trained models, but not usable in a scaffold-only agent.

source: Machine Mental Imagery: Mirage (2025)
finding: Letting a VLM emit latent 'visual' tokens mid-reasoning (no pixels) beats direct and text-CoT fine-tuning on spatial benchmarks.
numbers: Qwen2.5-VL-7B on VSP spatial reasoning: zero-shot .32, CoT SFT .84, Mirage CoT .87, Mirage+GRPO .89; spatial planning: Direct SFT .72, CoT SFT .47, Mirage Direct .76, Mirage CoT .58. Ablation planning: full .58, no stage 1 .52, no stage 2 .21. Latent size k=2 .86, 4 .87, 6 .88, 8 .75.
limits: Needs training. Text CoT hurt spatial planning (.72 to .47). Table column mapping partly ambiguous.
agent_relevance: Text chain-of-thought can hurt spatial planning; a no-CoT arm is worth keeping in the schema.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Visual Sketchpad
finding: An agent loop where the model draws sketches with code and tools (lines, plots, depth, crops) and looks at them improved GPT-4o on math and vision. This is an imagery method inside an LLM loop.
numbers: GPT-4o: max flow 25.0 to 66.3; graph isomorphism 50.8 to 65.3; geometry 62.5 to 66.7; parity 84.4 to 94.7; V*Bench 66.0 to 80.3; BLINK relative depth 71.8 to 83.9. GPT-4 Turbo parity fell 80.5 to 71.5. Humans drew the same auxiliary line as GPT-4o 80% of geometry cases. Cost per sample $0.011 to $0.133.
limits: Paper has internal inconsistencies (abstract 12.7% vs intro 11.2% math gain). Gains need good vision tools.
agent_relevance: Closest working example for O6: sketch with code, look, revise. Gains tied to computing the drawing in code, not asking the model to imagine.

source: Rahmanzadehgervi et al. (2024) Vision language models are blind
finding: VLMs fail on simple geometry that people see at a glance. Slow reasoning did not fix it, so the bottleneck is perception, not thought.
numbers: Mean accuracy over 7 tasks: Claude-3.5 Sonnet 77.84%, Gemini-1.5 Pro 58.48%, GPT-4o 50.23%, Claude-3 Sonnet 45.73%; chance 24%. Overlapping pentagons 30.99%, Olympic circles 39.44%. QVQ 42.48 vs Qwen2-VL 54.13; Gemini 2.0 Flash-Thinking 71.59 vs Flash 72.75.
limits: Synthetic, possibly out-of-distribution images. Page read through first 100k of 214k characters.
agent_relevance: Do not hand a picture to the model for a precise geometric fact; compute it from the data.

source: Xu et al. (2023) LLMs and ARC: object-based representations
finding: Row-by-row text serialisation breaks vertical objects. Giving GPT-4 objects instead of raw grids nearly doubles solves on simple tasks and removes the horizontal-vertical gap.
numbers: GPT-4 on 50 easy ARC tasks: raw grid 12-13; object JSON with CoT 23. Full 400 ARC training: 81 to 97. Mini-ARC 35 to 45 of 149. 1D-ARC: Move 3 Pixels 12 to 49; Fill vertical 1 to 49; Pile vertical 0 to 37. Of 13 raw-grid correct, only 3 had right reasoning; of 23 object-based, 20. GPT-4V solved 2 of 50. Adding edge info lowered scores.
limits: Only one abstraction method (ARGA best-fit). Subset of easiest tasks.
agent_relevance: Direct support for O6 in our ARC portfolio: change the form from pixel text to objects. Check reasoning, not only answers.

source: Fatemi et al. (2023) Talk like a Graph
finding: How a graph is written as text changes accuracy a lot; the best encoder differs by task. Headline gain 4.8% to 61.8%.
numbers: PaLM 62B zero-shot connected nodes: adjacency 19.8% vs incident 53.8%. Node degree CoT: incident 75.0. Cycle check zero-shot 76.0 vs zero-cot 32.3. Path graphs cycle check 5.9% vs complete graphs 91.7%. Application phrasing raised edge existence 42.8 to 60.8 (PaLM 2 XXS).
limits: PaLM models, not GPT. Several tasks below majority baselines. Zero-cot hurt on every task.
agent_relevance: Representation is a strong lever and task-dependent. Try 2-3 encodings and let code compare, do not pick one in advance.

source: Momennejad et al. (2023) CogEval: cognitive maps and planning in LLMs
finding: LLMs fail at planning on text-described graph worlds (cognitive-map tasks): invented edges, long paths, loops.
numbers: GPT-4 shortest path to state one cluster away: 0 of 30 at temperature 0. 1-step path score GPT-4 0.99, 3-step 0.55, policy revaluation 0.21. CoT raised non-teleport shortcut to 1.00 (GPT-4, GPT-3.5) but davinci-003 fell 0.49 to 0.09. BFS/DFS instructions helped inconsistently.
limits: Scores are ARI-like per Table 3 caption; text gives no exact BFS numbers.
agent_relevance: Do the graph search in code. The model should not hold a map in its head.

source: Wang et al. (2025) MindCube
finding: Asking a model to first write a cognitive map, then reason over it, lifts accuracy on spatial questions from limited views.
numbers: 21,154 questions over 3,268 images; baseline near random. Map-then-reason 37.8% to 57.8% (+20.0); with RL 61.3% (+23.5).
limits: Abstract page only; training used.
agent_relevance: Written map as an intermediate state, a symbolic stand-in for an image. Fits S-state design.

source: Abdou et al. (2021) Can language models encode perceptual structure without grounding?
finding: Text-only models carry some structure of color space, information imagery theorists thought needed a picture-like code. Weak support for the propositional side.
numbers: Kendall tau (max over layers): BERT .26, RoBERTa .33, ELECTRA .25; linear mapping selectivity ~.75-.78. fastText tau .23; pmi-3 .17. BERT base CC tau .162 vs mini .077. Shuffled controls: none significant. Only 18 color terms.
limits: Small vocabulary. Alignment weak and incomplete; authors say full isomorphism is unlikely.
agent_relevance: Text-only models are not blank on perceptual structure, but alignment is partial; do not trust it for fine perception.

source: Synthesis: symbolic recoding works, true transformation fails (our reading of c08, c10, c12, c15, c17)
finding: Across studies, models do well when spatial info can be recoded as symbols or objects and badly when real transformation (rotation, motion) is needed. This resembles the propositional side of the imagery debate, but the data do not settle it for humans.
numbers: Cube Rolling 97.5-98.3% vs Mental Rotation 4.5-20.5% (SpatiaLite); rotation 56.7% vs human 79.6%; 3D rotation 50% vs human 79.16%.
limits: Our synthesis, not a source claim. Different benchmarks and models.
agent_relevance: Rule for O6: recode into objects or coordinates and compute in code; use pictures for model-visible layout only with a measured gain.

source: Synthesis: drawn state helps only if correct (our reading of c01-c03, c05, c15)
finding: Methods that make the model draw its state help most when tracking is long or exact lookup is hard, and only when the drawing is correct.
numbers: VoT: correct decisions 65-77% given accurate drawing, drawing accurate only 24-26% of the time. FrozenLake CoT errors 90.8% from wrong hole coordinates. Sketchpad max flow +41.3 points.
limits: Cross-paper synthesis; not one controlled study.
agent_relevance: Make code produce and verify the drawn state (G2, G3). Free-hand model drawings are unreliable.

source: Synthesis: scaffold-only versus trained pictorial reasoning (our reading of c13, c14)
finding: Pictorial reasoning wins in trained models on larger grids (VPRL 82.4 vs Gemini 2.5 Pro 38.8 at 6x6), while text tricks (ASCII, coordinates) reach 73-74 under SFT.
numbers: FrozenLake SFT: direct 68.6, coordinates 74.4, ASCII 73.1; VPRL 91.6.
limits: Trained systems cannot be used in a no-training scaffold.
agent_relevance: For a scaffold-only agent, ASCII or coordinate grids are the achievable part of O6; picture generation is out of scope.

source: Synthesis: text chain-of-thought can hurt spatial tasks (our reading of c11, c14, c18)
finding: Several studies show chain-of-thought can lower spatial scores, so extra verbal steps should not be forced on spatial tasks.
numbers: VisFactor: CoT hurt P3, CS2, SS3, VZ1. Mirage: CoT SFT planning .47 vs direct .72. Talk like a Graph: zero-cot below zero-shot on all 6 tasks. Overlapping numerosity: CoT 41.3 vs NoCoT 43.9.
limits: Mixed model families and tasks.
agent_relevance: Keep a no-CoT arm in representation-change tests.
